text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- NATIONAL MONETARY COUNCIL REDUCES PROFITS FROM SAVINGS
Brazil's National Monetary Council yesterday announced it will raise the referential rate (TR) reducer for 1997's first three months, which will lower the profitability of savings accounts.
-- BANKS SEEK TOTAL CONTROL OVER DEBTORS
Brazilian banks, whose federation meets today with Central Bank officials, are seeking new tools to revive credit transactions with greater security.
-- BRAZIL'S CEF STILL LACKS FOUR BILLION REAIS
The Brazilian government's Caixa Economica Federal still does not have the four billion reais announced earlier this week for new home financing for the middle class.
O GLOBO
-- U.S. PROHIBITS ARMS SALES THAT SUPPLY RIO TRAFFICKERS
The United States yesterday suspended arms licenses to export arms and munitions to Paraguay, which supplies 70 percent of the illegal arms flooding Rio de Janeiro.
-- ELECTRICAL ENERGY WILL RISE IN RIO IN NOVEMBER
Recently privatized Light power utility will adjust electrical energy rates in November, as outlined in the concession contract, according to company President Michel Gaillard.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- PROFITS FROM SAVINGS ACCOUNTS TO FALL IN 1997

The profitability of savings accounts will be reduced in the January-March period next year. The government yesterday decided to raise referential rate (TR) reducer to 0.97 percent in January from 0.85 percent in December.
-- GOVERNMENT READIES 8 MILLION-REAI PUBLICITY CAMPAIGN

Brazilian government officials are readying an eight million-reai publicity campaign to highlight the works and deeds of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's administration. The campaign will coincide with Congressional debate on a bill to allow Cardoso to run for a second term.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
